One of my Fort Wayne clients spends about $15 a day on Google Ads. Last month that brought in 12 leads at roughly $37 each.

A small budget can absolutely work. When it does not, the problem is almost always the setup, not the money. Display network left on by default, ad clicks going to the homepage instead of the right page, no conversion tracking to show what is actually working.

A client of mine runs Google Ads on $15 a day. Last month: 12 leads, about $37 each.

I share this because I hear "we're too small for Google Ads" constantly, and it is usually not true. What actually holds small accounts back is the setup:

- The Display Network and Search Partners left on by default, spending on the wrong placements
- Ad traffic pointed at the homepage instead of a page about the specific service
- No conversion tracking, so there is no way to know what is working

Fix those and a small budget goes a lot further. Full breakdown, including a change coming to Google's bidding on August 17 that affects budget-limited campaigns: https://brightboxdigital.io/blog/does-a-small-google-ads-budget-work/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=blog_bbx001
